# Codemap - issue 0147, round 14: the pinned gap `self-scope-max-house-rules`

The issue fences the scope hard: only `src/evaluator/` production code and its
unit tests may change. Nothing under `docs/testing/` is touched - its `.ros`
files, `scenario.json` and `README.md` are the specification, and
`docs/testing/campaign-state.json` belongs to the campaign driver, not to this
fix.

What the scenario demands, in one sentence: a `max` constraint with
`scope="self"` makes its own carrier selection the counting frame and counts the
selections underneath it, so `714b-5314-33d4-dd68` on `Allow Mercenaries`
(`fda5-49b9-b74c-aaf4`) must fire with actual 2 against bound 1 in rosters 01 and
06 and stay silent in 02-05.

The run has closed this map: the increment `self-scope-max-frame` was accepted,
and the list below is what it actually touched. Nothing in the issue is left
open, so the map is a record rather than a forecast.

## Changed by the run

- `src/evaluator/constraints.js` - turns each declared limit into a count query
  and a violation; it is where a limit's scope, counted target and flags are
  bound before the count is asked, and where the `self`-scoped `max` is decided.
- `src/evaluator/query.js` - the single counting primitive: resolves a scope
  keyword to its frame node and reads that frame's tally, including the gate
  that decides when the frame's own share belongs to the answer.
- `src/evaluator/countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js` - its control case pinned
  the reading the scenario refutes and was rewritten to the new one.
- `src/evaluator/constraints.selfScopeFrame.test.js` - added by the run; pins the
  counting frame, the piece count, the depth flag and the `min` side.
- `src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md` - the evaluator's living rule notes; every round of
  this issue records its counting-frame decision here.

## Proved untouched by the run

These were on the map as candidates and turned out not to need changing; they
are named here so a later round does not re-open them without a reason.

- `src/evaluator/countIndex.js` - the per-frame tallies and the frame-own slot
  already carried what the fix needed; the gate that reads them landed in
  `query.js` instead.
- `src/evaluator/model.js` - the scope keywords and limit/flag shapes expressed
  the needed distinction already; the new gate is engine-own, not a written flag.
- `src/evaluator/countIndex.costSumCarrierFrame.test.js`,
  `src/evaluator/query.matrix.test.js`, `src/evaluator/constraints.test.js`,
  `src/evaluator/constraints.carrierDescendants.test.js`,
  `src/evaluator/violationClassification.test.js` - all stayed green unchanged, so
  the fix contradicted none of the behaviour they pin.

## Read-only, the specification and the check surface

- `docs/testing/self-scope-max-house-rules/` - `README.md`, `scenario.json` and
  the six `rosters/*.ros`: the specification, never edited.
- `src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js` - the manifest-driven runner that
  executes the scenario under `npx vitest run src/evaluator`; not changed by this
  issue.
- `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` - the frozen catalog data the
  scenario reads (`.gst` plus the Ogre Kingdoms and Mercenaries `.cat`); never
  edited.

## Campaign bookkeeping the issue puts out of scope

The review observed that `docs/testkatalog-evaluator-e2e.md` still describes the
scenario as red and `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` still lists it under
`pinnedGaps`. Both files sit outside the fence the issue draws and are the
campaign driver's to update, not this issue's.

increments.title: A self-scoped max counts what stands under its carrier
increments.goal: Make `docs/testing/self-scope-max-house-rules` green in all six of its cases. A `max` constraint with `scope="self"` must take its own carrier selection as the counting frame and count the selections underneath it - with `includeChildSelections="false"`, its direct children. So `714b-5314-33d4-dd68` on `Allow Mercenaries` (`fda5-49b9-b74c-aaf4`) fires with actual 2 against bound 1 both when the carrier holds its two hidden house-rule children (`713c-28b1-0861-1ffd`, `698e-c660-5c99-d481`) and when it holds a single child node with `number="2"`, and stays silent at 1 or 0 children. Today it fires in none of the six rosters, so the limit is not merely counting in the wrong frame - it never speaks at all. Roster 05 delimits the frame from the outside: there the PARENT entry holds two direct children while the carrier holds one, and the limit must stay silent, so counting in the parent frame is not the fix. The whole issue is this one change; it is not split, because the two red cases are two readings of one counting rule and neither stands as a reviewable change on its own.
criteria: `npx vitest run src/evaluator` passes all six cases of `docs/testing/self-scope-max-house-rules`.

In `rosters/01-both-house-rules-self-max-fires.ros` and `rosters/06-single-house-rule-number-two-self-max-fires.ros` the report carries a violation for limit `714b-5314-33d4-dd68` with actual 2 and bound 1.

In `rosters/02`, `03`, `04` and `05` no violation for `714b-5314-33d4-dd68` is reported - roster 05 in particular, where the carrier's parent holds two direct children and the carrier itself holds one.
The parent-scoped sibling limit `1df9-8159-156a-641f` is absent from the report in all six rosters.
`npx vitest run src/evaluator` exits 0 with no failing case anywhere else in the evaluator suite - every scenario green before the change is green after it.
Only files under `src/evaluator/` are changed; nothing under `docs/testing/` is modified, added or deleted.

return.plan:
## What is wrong today

`src/evaluator/constraints.js` -> `evaluateLimit` (line ~106) counts, for EVERY limit, the **carrier's own resolved target id** inside the limit's frame:

```js
const targetId = isLinkDefinition(node.def) ? node.def.targetId : node.def.id;
const actual = query(ctx, limit.field, limit.scope, targetId, countingFlagsOf(limit, node));
```

For `scope="parent"` that is right (`1df9-8159-156a-641f` counts how many `Allow Mercenaries` stand under `6a7d-...` -> 1, silent, correct today). For `scope="self"` the frame IS the carrier (`query.js` -> `resolveSharedFrame`, `case ScopeKeyword.SELF: return ctx.node`), so the engine asks "how many occurrences of the carrier stand inside the carrier" and, through the count index, gets back the carrier's own `number`. In all six rosters `Allow Mercenaries` has `number="1"`, so `714b-5314-33d4-dd68` reads actual 1 against bound 1 and never speaks. That is why the limit is silent in rosters 01 and 06 rather than counting in the wrong frame.

What the data demands (`docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §7.6, rule box: "**Gezaehlt werden die Auswahlen *unterhalb* des Traegers der Grenze**, nicht der Traeger selbst. Der `scope` sagt nur, in welchem Rahmen summiert wird"): with the carrier as the frame, the counted set is what stands under it - with `includeChildSelections="false"` its direct children, counted by piece (`number`), not by node.

## The change

Two files, both under `src/evaluator/`.

### 1. `src/evaluator/constraints.js` - decide the counted target and the frame-own gate

In `evaluateLimit`, a limit that is **`scope="self"` AND `field.kind === CountedFieldKind.SELECTION_COUNT`** counts the frame's contents instead of the carrier's occurrences:

- the query target becomes `null` ("everything in the frame") instead of the carrier's resolved target id;
- the flags handed to `query` are the written flags (i.e. what `countingFlagsOf(limit, node)` returns - it passes SELF through untouched, it only lifts ROSTER/FORCE) **plus** the engine-own gate `includeFrameOwn: false`, so the carrier's own count stays out of the answer (§7.6: "nicht der Traeger selbst"). Build a new object; never mutate `limit.flags`.
- `countedTargetId` in the returned result **keeps the carrier's resolved target id**, unchanged. That field is the identity of the obligation across anchors and the dedup key in `report.js` (lines 189 and 279) - it is not the query's filter. Both dedup paths only touch synthetic category anchors and mandatory entry phantoms at roster/force scope, so a SELF result at an OCCUPIED anchor is untouched either way; keeping the carrier id is the smaller change and stays honest about "whose limit this is".

Suggested shape (names are free, the behaviour is not):

```js
const countsFrameContents = limit.scope === ScopeKeyword.SELF
  && limit.field.kind === CountedFieldKind.SELECTION_COUNT;
const countingFlags = countingFlagsOf(limit, node);
const actual = query(
  ctx,
  limit.field,
  limit.scope,
  countsFrameContents ? null : targetId,
  countsFrameContents ? { ...countingFlags, includeFrameOwn: false } : countingFlags,
);
```

`CountedFieldKind` must be added to the `./model.js` import list in `constraints.js` (`ScopeKeyword` is already imported).

Record the decision in the JSDoc of `evaluateLimit` (and/or a sibling helper), in English, next to the existing block that explains why a link's resolved target id is counted: name §7.6, name the counting frame, and name the two rosters that delimit it (05 = not the parent frame, 02 = not the carrier itself).

### 2. `src/evaluator/query.js` - make the frame-own gate overridable

`query` currently hands `frame === ctx.node` to `index.get` as the fifth argument (line ~453). Make it an engine-own flag with an unchanged default, exactly like the existing `includeClimbedCosts` precedent one line above:

```js
flags?.includeFrameOwn ?? (frame === ctx.node),
```

Read it from the **raw** `flags`, not from `normalizeFlags(flags)` - that helper returns only the three Battlescribe flags and would drop it (same reason `includeClimbedCosts` is read raw). Extend the `@param flags` JSDoc of `query` to document the new gate: "the frame node's own share under the `null` target; without an entry it follows `frame === ctx.node`. The constraint layer closes it for a `scope=\"self\"` selection-count limit, which counts what stands *under* its carrier (§7.6)."

No other file needs a change: `countIndex.js` already carries the `FRAME_OWN` slot and the `includeFrameOwn` parameter of `get`; `model.js` already carries `ScopeKeyword.SELF` and `CountedFieldKind.SELECTION_COUNT`.

## Why the counting comes out right

In the count index (`countIndex.js` -> `indexNodeContribution`) a node's own count lands, in its **own** frame under the `null` target, in the separate `FRAME_OWN` slot; its direct children land in `Bucket.BASE`; grandchildren in `Bucket.SELECTION`. So with target `null`, `includeChildSelections=false` and `includeFrameOwn=false`, the answer is exactly "the sum of the `number`s of the direct children":

- roster 01: 713c(1) + 698e(1) = **2** > 1 -> fires, actual 2 / bound 1;
- roster 06: 713c(2) = **2** > 1 -> fires (piece count, not node count - the index adds `instance.count`);
- rosters 02, 03: one child, 1 -> silent; roster 04: no child, 0 -> silent;
- roster 05: the carrier holds one child -> 1 -> silent, while the parent `6a7d-...` holding two children is a different frame key and is never consulted;
- `1df9-8159-156a-641f` (`scope="parent"`) is not touched by the change at all and keeps reading 1 -> stays absent in all six.

Offer anchors and phantoms are synthetic and never enter the index (`countIndex.buildIndex` iterates `realNodes`), so the two hidden, unselected house rules add nothing in rosters 04 and 05. `hidden="true"` does not remove a selected node from the index either, so the two hidden children do count in roster 01 (§5.6/§8: max limits apply regardless of visibility).

## Decisions taken, and what was rejected

- **Restricted to `field="selections"`.** A `scope="self"` limit on a **cost** field keeps today's reading (the carrier's own costs under `includeChildSelections="false"`, plus climbed descendant costs under `true`) - a separate, settled rule from Issues 091/0113, pinned by `countIndex.costSumCarrierFrame.test.js`. Switching the target to `null` for cost fields would add the carrier's own costs to the descendants' and break that file (50 + 60 = 110 against 100). `FORCE_COUNT` and `LIMIT_VALUE` are untouched for the same reason (`LIMIT_VALUE` never reaches the frame code at all).
- **Decided in the constraint layer, not in `query.js` by scope alone.** The primitive cannot tell a constraint's "everything under the carrier" from a **condition** with `scope="self"` and `childId="any"`/no `childId`, which must keep reading the carrier's own count - pinned by `countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js` lines 370-384 and used by real catalogue data. The constraint layer is where the counted target is chosen anyway.
- **Not the parent frame.** Roster 05 forbids it (parent holds two direct children, the limit must stay silent).
- **The carrier's own count stays out.** Roster 02 forbids including it (carrier 1 + child 1 = 2 would fire against bound 1). Roster 04 alone would not settle this, since 1 <= 1 is silent too.
- **Min limits follow the same frame rule.** §7.6 states the counting rule without distinguishing `min` from `max`, and a kind-specific counting frame would be an invention. Checked consequences: `violationClassification.test.js` (`min-self` value 9 on a warrior of count 3 holding one shield: actual 3 -> 1, still below 9, still reported, and every assertion there is about message shape) and `offer.test.js` (`min` self at an unselected offer anchor: 0 -> 0) stay green.
- **The percent denominator is left alone.** `resolveBound` keeps reading `query(ctx, limit.field, limit.scope, null, limit.flags)` with the written flags and the default frame-own gate - a documented decision of that function ("der Nenner zaehlt 'alles im Rahmen' stets mit den hingeschriebenen Flags"). No `percentValue="true"` selection limit with `scope="self"` exists in the fixture data, and changing it would risk the pinned percent control in `countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js` (line 260) for no data-backed gain. Out of this increment's scope.

## The one existing case that this change refutes

`src/evaluator/countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js`, case at line 229, `KONTROLLE: eine scope="self"-Grenze zaehlt weiterhin ihren eigenen Rahmen`: an entry with `max 1 field="selections" scope="self"`, selected with `count: 2` and **no children**, expects a violation of actual 2 / bound 1. Under the new rule that count is 0 and the limit is silent. That case pins the very reading the black-box scenario refutes (the issue: "the scenario is the specification and the engine is what is wrong"), so it is rewritten, not preserved - see the test plan. The implementer does not touch it; it will be red between the two steps and that is expected.

I checked every other user of `scope="self"` in the suite (`countIndex.costSumCarrierFrame`, `countIndex.linkedType`, `infoProjection`, `offer`, `query.limitValue`, `query.matrix`, `report`, `violationClassification`): all are either conditions, cost fields, direct `query` calls with an explicit target, or min limits that keep their verdict. This is the only contradicted case.

## Scope fence

Only `src/evaluator/` changes. Nothing under `docs/testing/` is edited - not the six rosters, not `scenario.json`, not `README.md`, not `campaign-state.json`. `docs/evaluator-architecture.md` mentions the self frame only for climbed costs (line 520), which this change does not touch, and it lies outside the fence anyway; no ADR states what a self-scoped constraint counts (ADR 0029 only fixes `self` = the one carrying instance as the frame, which stays true), so nothing needs flagging.

- `src/evaluator/constraints.js` - the constraint layer. `evaluateLimit` (line ~106) picks the counted target id and the flags and calls `query`; **the entry point of this change**. `countingFlagsOf` (line ~91) is the existing precedent for a scope-dependent flag adjustment; `resolveBound` (line ~40) reads the percent denominator and is left alone; `evaluateConstraints` (line ~188) is the loop over all nodes and limits.
- `src/evaluator/query.js` - the single counting primitive. `query` (line ~400) resolves the frame via `resolveFrame`/`resolveSharedFrame` (lines ~205/~169, `SELF -> ctx.node`) and passes `frame === ctx.node` as the frame-own gate into `index.get` (line ~448-454); that gate becomes overridable via `flags.includeFrameOwn`, read from the raw flags like the neighbouring `includeClimbedCosts`.
- `src/evaluator/countIndex.js` - builds the per-frame tallies. `FRAME_OWN` (line ~60) is the frame node's own share under the `null` target, `Bucket.BASE` holds the frame's direct children, `Bucket.SELECTION` the deeper ones; `combineBuckets` (line ~331) and `buildIndex().get` (line ~377) already take `includeFrameOwn`. **No edit needed** - the codemap lists it as likely to change; it is not.
- `src/evaluator/model.js` - `ScopeKeyword.SELF` (line ~130), `CountedFieldKind.SELECTION_COUNT` / `SELECTION_COUNT` (lines ~41/48), `normalizeFlags` (line ~184, returns only the three Battlescribe flags - hence the new gate must be read from the raw flags). **No edit needed**; the codemap's "touched only if" does not apply.
- `src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md` - **codemap correction**: this is the *test-suite* doc (vitest conventions, JSDOM setup, facade-driven tests, German titles, the `KONTROLLE:` marker), not a rule-notes file, and no earlier round recorded a counting-frame decision in it. The counting-frame decisions live in the module JSDoc of `constraints.js`, `query.js` and `countIndex.js`; record this one there. Do not edit `CLAUDE.md` for the production change.
- `src/evaluator/countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js` - holds the single case this change refutes (line 229) and the two `scope="self"` **condition** controls that must stay green (lines 370-384), plus the percent-denominator control (line 260) and the `scope="force" childId="any"` control (line 304).
- `src/evaluator/countIndex.costSumCarrierFrame.test.js` - pins the self-scoped **cost** reading under both `includeChildSelections` settings (lines 120-140); the reason the fix is restricted to `SELECTION_COUNT`. Unchanged.

That is why no other committed E2E scenario can be affected: the other rosters that hold `Allow Mercenaries` (`docs/testing/violation-classification/rosters/07-...`, `docs/testing/offer-and-category-slots/rosters/01-...` and `02-...`) hold it childless, so the limit reads 0 there and stays silent. return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. The six E2E cases are already committed under `docs/testing/self-scope-max-house-rules/` and are executed by the manifest runner inside `npx vitest run src/evaluator`; **write no E2E scenario and touch nothing under `docs/testing/`**. The test work is one rewritten unit case plus one new unit file.

## Conventions

The suite doc is `src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md` and it exists, is current, and matches what I read in the files (JSDOM `DOMParser` at module top, drive the engine through `prepareDataset` + `evaluate`, nothing mocked, inline synthetic catalogues or a per-file catalogue factory, German `describe`/`it` titles, English code comments, `KONTROLLE:` in the title of a case that pins already-correct behaviour). Load it and follow it; I found nothing in it that contradicts this plan, so nothing in it needs correcting.

## What to test, per acceptance criterion

**Criteria 1-4 (the six scenario cases, the two firing limits, the four silent rosters, the absent parent-scoped sibling)** are covered by the committed scenario through the manifest runner. No new test is written for them; they are the reason the check command is the whole evaluator directory.

**Criterion 5 (nothing else in the suite goes red)** needs one existing case rewritten, because the change deliberately refutes it, and the new rule pinned at unit level so a later round cannot silently undo it.

### A. Rewrite the one contradicted case

File: `src/evaluator/countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js`, the case at line 229, currently `it('KONTROLLE: eine scope="self"-Grenze zaehlt weiterhin ihren eigenen Rahmen', ...)`.

Its catalogue (entry `entry-self-scope`, `type="unit"`, one `constraint id="limit-self-scope" type="max" value="1" field="selections" scope="self"`, no children) with a roster selecting it `count: 2` expects today a violation with `actual: 2, bound: 1`. Under the new rule the self frame holds no selections, the count is 0 and the limit is silent.

Keep the catalogue and the roster; invert the assertion and retitle the case, for example `KONTROLLE: eine scope="self"-Grenze zaehlt die Auswahlen UNTER ihrem Traeger, nicht dessen eigenen Bestand` asserting `expect(report.violations.find(violation => violation.limitId === SELF_SCOPE_LIMIT_ID)).toBeUndefined()`. Add an English comment naming this increment as the round that changed the reading, and pointing at `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §7.6 ("counted are the selections *beneath* the limit's carrier, not the carrier itself") and at `docs/testing/self-scope-max-house-rules` roster 02 as the case that forbids counting the carrier.

The other four control cases in that file must stay untouched and green - they are what keeps the fix out of `query.js`'s general behaviour:
- line 260, percent limit on a cost field at `scope="roster"` (frame's own share stays in the denominator),
- line 304, `scope="force" childId="any"`,
- lines 370 and 377, a **condition** with `scope="self"` and no `childId`, which still reads the carrier's own count.

### B. New unit file for the rule

File: `src/evaluator/constraints.selfScopeFrame.test.js` (the constraint layer owns the rule; `<module>.<topic>.test.js` per the suite doc). Level: the public facade (`prepareDataset` + `evaluate` from `./evaluator.js`) against a small synthetic catalogue built by a per-file factory - the rule is observable as a violation, and no fixture parse is needed. Framework: vitest. Command that runs just this file: `npx vitest run src/evaluator/constraints.selfScopeFrame.test.js`.

Skeleton the cases share: a force, a `PARENT` entry holding a `CARRIER` entry and a `SIBLING` entry; the `CARRIER` carries `max 1 field="selections" scope="self" shared="true" includeChildSelections="false"` and offers two child entries `CHILD_A` and `CHILD_B`; `CHILD_A` offers one grandchild `GRANDCHILD`. Vary only the roster (and, in case 6, the one flag). Assert against `report.violations` filtered by `limitId`.

1. **Two direct children fire.** Carrier `count: 1` holding `CHILD_A` (1) and `CHILD_B` (1) -> a violation for the self limit with `actual: 2, bound: 1`. (Mirrors scenario roster 01.)
2. **Piece count, not node count.** Carrier `count: 1` holding only `CHILD_A` with `count: 2` -> a violation with `actual: 2, bound: 1`. (Mirrors roster 06 and §7.5.)
3. **One child stays silent.** Carrier `count: 1` holding `CHILD_A` (1) -> no violation for that limit. (Mirrors rosters 02/03; this is the case that forbids adding the carrier's own count.)
4. **Zero point, and the carrier does not count itself.** Carrier selected with `count: 2` and no children -> no violation. State in an English comment that a reading which counted the carrier's own stock would report actual 2 here; this case replaces the reading rewritten in A.
5. **The parent frame is not the counting frame.** `PARENT` holds two direct children (`CARRIER` and `SIBLING`), the carrier holds one child -> no violation. (Mirrors roster 05.)
6. **The depth flag decides what "underneath" means.** Same roster (carrier -> `CHILD_A` -> `GRANDCHILD`, each `count: 1`) evaluated twice: with `includeChildSelections="false"` the count is 1 and the limit stays silent; with `includeChildSelections="true"` it is 2 and the limit fires with `actual: 2, bound: 1`. The scenario deliberately could not pin this (its README, "Bewusst nicht geprueft": the two house rules have no grandchildren in the data), so it is pinned here instead.
7. **A min limit uses the same frame.** A second carrier entry with `min 1 field="selections" scope="self"`, selected once and holding no child -> a violation with `actual: 0, bound: 1`; the same entry holding one child -> silent. This pins the decision that the frame rule is a counting rule, not a `max`-only rule.

Write the titles in German, the code comments in English, and mark none of these `KONTROLLE:` - they pin new behaviour and are expected to be red before the production change.

### Deliberately not tested

- **The `scope="self"` cost reading** - unchanged by the fix and already pinned by `countIndex.costSumCarrierFrame.test.js`; a second copy would only drift.
- **A `scope="self"` condition without `childId`** - unchanged and already pinned at `countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js` lines 370-384; that pair is exactly the guard against moving the fix into `query.js`.
- **A percent (`percentValue="true"`) self-scoped selection limit** - no such shape exists in the catalogue data and the denominator is deliberately left as it is (see the plan's rejected options); pinning an untouched corner would fix behaviour nobody decided.
- **`shared="false"` with `scope="self"`** - the frame resolves to the same node either way, so it adds no distinction to observe.

## What counts as done

Exactly one command, run from the repository root, and nothing else:

- `npx vitest run src/evaluator`

It is the issue's own check command, it covers the manifest-driven E2E runner over all of `docs/testing/` together with every unit and layer test in the directory, and the change touches nothing outside `src/evaluator/`. No linter, formatter, type check or app E2E run belongs to this increment.

## What is already red
